title: ephemeral-playbook-signer-and-suppression-ledger-for-temporary-runs
author: Ava Patel
description: Context: On-call teams often create temporary ad-hoc playbooks or tweak runbooks during incidents. These transient playbooks are valuable for fast mitigation but are hard to audit and can be a vector for accidental or malicious misconfiguration. Motivation: provide an auditable, short-lived playbook signing mechanism plus a suppression ledger that records alert suppression windows and their provenance. Goals: 1) Allow engineers to create ephemeral playbooks that are cryptographically signed and automatically expire; 2) Record every suppression (manual or API) in a ledger that preserves who requested it, the reason, link to signed playbook (if applicable), and automatic expiry; 3) Surface ledger entries in the incident timeline and export to audit logs; 4) Offer CLI helpers and a small UI surface to create/surface signed playbooks and suppression entries. High-level change summary: - New signing service (playbook-signer) that integrates with customer or Redwood KMS (pluggable) and issues short-lived signatures embedded in playbook metadata. Signed playbooks can be verified by the incident-bot runtime before execution. - Suppression ledger API + storage: append-only ledger (Postgres-backed using existing eventstore pattern) with strict write paths: api, cli, and authorized webhook. Ledger entries include origin, signer id (if playbook-signed), suppression window, and optional runbook_id. - Feature-flag guarded rollout: incident_bot.features.ephemeral_signing and .suppression_ledger. Defaults off in main, enabled for beta orgs. - CLI: rb-sign and rb-suppress commands to create signed playbooks and ledger entries; output includes signed manifest and human-readable audit line. - UI: small addition to incident detail pane showing active suppressions and a link to download the signed playbook manifest. - Migration: adds a new table suppression_ledger_v1 and a compact index for query by active window. Migration script included. - Tests: unit coverage for signer, ledger append and verification; integration test exercising end-to-end: create signed playbook -> verify -> execute guarded run -> ledger entry created and surfaced to timeline. - Security: signing keys go through KMS abstraction; private key material never stored by incident-bot. Signing operations are performed by a short-lived token service; audit events emitted to the existing audit pipeline. - Backwards compatibility: unsigned playbooks still accepted if feature flag off; when on, unverified playbooks are rejected for orgs that opted into enforcement. - Docs: commands, API endpoints, feature flag instructions, and rollback steps included in docs/operations/ephemeral-playbooks.md. Rollout plan: staged across beta orgs for 2 weeks, gather telemetry on acceptance rates and any failed verifications, then widen. Migration note: migration creates table and index and backfills no data; suppression ledger relies on append-only writes and uses existing housekeeping for TTL on expired entries. Risks and mitigations: potential false positives if clocks drift (mitigated by allowing 30s skew and validating at KMS layer); extra latency on playbook execution when signature verification runs (measured ~12ms in p99 on staging, acceptable).

release_notes: Added ephemeral playbook signing and an append-only suppression ledger. Operators can create signed, time-limited playbooks and record suppressions with provenance. Feature behind flags: incident_bot.features.ephemeral_signing and incident_bot.features.suppression_ledger. CLI tools (rb-sign/rb-suppress) and a small UI card are included. Backwards-compatible by default. See docs/operations/ephemeral-playbooks.md for rollout and rollback steps.
